newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian deficit to force more belt-tightening.
newsitem.headline: Colombian deficit to force more belt-tightening.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 18 Reuter - The Colombian government's burgeoning fiscal deficit will force it to adopt harsh economic belt-tightening measures in the months ahead, including an austere budget for 1998, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said.

Ocampo, who spoke at an annual meeting of the National Exporters' Association ANALDEX late Thursday, said that without counting privatization revenues the central government's deficit was expected to rise to 4.1 percent of gross domestic product this year, up from 3.3 percent in 1996.

He said the government hoped to cut it by two percentage points before President Ernesto Samper leaves office next year, but this would require sharp reductions in public spending, including financing of provincial governments.
"There will be an austere budget for 1998," Ocampo said, vowing to put the government's economic house in order before Samper hands over power in August 1998.

"The two-point reduction of the deficit should come from less spending and more revenues," Ocampo said, adding that curbs would be placed on tax evasion and Colombia's booming trade in contraband goods as part of efforts to shore up government finances.
